title: Breathers in solitonic room-temperature superlattice-induced superfluorescence in quasi-2D perovskites
authors: A. A. Gladkij, N. N. Rosanov, B. D. Fainberg
abstract: Recently, a soliton mechanism for room-temperature superfluorescence in thin perovskite films has been proposed, with a fundamental soliton predicted to remain stable under LO phonon--exciton interactions. At the same time, superlattice architectures offer a route to enhancing superfluorescence in perovskites. Motivated by recent observations of room-temperature superfluorescence in periodic superlattices of quasi-2D metal-halide perovskites, we extend the 2D nonlocal nonlinear Schrödinger equation describing Wannier exciton--LO phonon interactions to superlattice structures, obtaining a 3D nonlocal nonlinear Schrödinger equation. We show that interlayer tunnelling gives rise to breather dynamics corresponding to a stable fundamental soliton in mixed coordinate--momentum space, with the coordinate parallel to the layers and the momentum perpendicular to them. The breather dynamics originate from miniband formation, which induces a momentum-dependent phase modulation of the soliton. In the absence of interlayer tunnelling, the breather dynamics disappear and the soliton becomes stationary. These results establish a direct connection between interlayer tunnelling, miniband formation and soliton dynamics, suggesting that breather behavior can provide a signature of interlayer tunnelling in quasi-2D perovskite superlattices.
summary: This theoretical study models superfluorescence in perovskite superlattices, showing that interlayer tunneling introduces a new degree of freedom via miniband formation. This coupling causes the fundamental soliton solution to evolve into a stable breather state, providing a measurable signature of the interlayer coupling strength.
main_problem: The study investigates the origin of stable macroscopic quantum coherence at room temperature in quasi-2D perovskites, specifically focusing on how interlayer coupling modifies superfluorescence dynamics.
main_result: Interlayer tunneling induces miniband formation, which causes the fundamental soliton to exhibit breather dynamics—a coherent temporal redistribution of the exciton amplitude among the layers. This breather behavior is absent when tunneling is removed.
method: The analysis extends the 2D nonlinear Schrödinger equation to a 3D nonlocal form for superlattices, using approximations like the adiabatic limit and Fourier transforms in momentum space.
model_or_system: The system models Wannier exciton–LO phonon interactions in quasi-2D metal-halide perovskite superlattices. The dynamics are governed by a 3D nonlocal nonlinear Schrödinger equation derived from the exciton-phonon Hamiltonian.
key_observables: Breather dynamics (temporal oscillations of exciton amplitude), the fundamental soliton profile, and the resulting miniband dispersion.
important_parameters: Interlayer coupling strength ($J$), number of layers ($	ilde{N}$), and the in-plane momentum ($q$).
main_assumptions: The derivation relies on the adiabatic approximation, the single-exciton wavefunction approximation, and assuming the ground-state population remains near unity.

paper_structure: The paper builds from the initial 2D description to a 3D nonlocal NLS equation for superlattices. It then analyzes the role of interlayer tunneling, showing how miniband formation introduces a phase modulation that manifests as coherent breather dynamics, contrasting this with the stationary soliton found when tunneling is zero.
why_interesting: This work directly connects solid-state physics (perovskites, superlattices) with nonlinear wave phenomena (solitons, breathers) in a quantum optical context, providing a mechanism (miniband formation) to generate complex, observable dynamics from simple structural periodicity.
